newsitem.title: UK: Tokyo stocks drop, London posts modest gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks drop, London posts modest gains.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.

LONDON - British shares closed higher for a third successive day, rebounding from early U.S.-led weakness and extending gains on relief that U.S. employment data turned up few surprises about inflationary pressures. The FTSE 100 index finished up 5.8 points at 3,893.0, up 25.3 from last week.

FRANKFURT - German blue chip shares ended bourse trade lower, undermined by the sharp overnight fall on Wall Street and amid uncertainty ahead of the U.S. jobs data due later in the day. The DAX index of Germany's 30 leading shares closed 12.54 points or 0.50 percent lower at 2,517.00, down 26.83 from last Friday. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,542.74.

PARIS - French stocks finished higher, buoyed by helpful U.S. data and better-than-expected corporate results. "If the results keep coming out this way, the market could get a real bounce," one trader said after a string of companies reported big profit gains for the first half. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 8.52 points or 0.43 percent to 2,004.75, rising 34.14 from seven days ago.

ZURICH - Swiss shares prices rose late in the day to end higher, supported by a better Wall Street opening and short covering, U.S. employement data, which was better than expected, did not have much effect, although the data did not soften interest rate fears, one trader noted, trade was generally quiet. The All-share Swiss Performance Index rose 6.83 points or 0.29 percent to close at 2,332.73, falling 10.26 on the week.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks tumbled by the end of the Friday session, following a sharp slide on Wall Street overnight, the Tokyo market was bracing for the U.S. August employment report to be released later today. The key 225-share Nikkei average closed down 227.29 points or 1.12 percent at 20,152.53, a drop of 14.37 on the week.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks slumbered to a lower close, with investors cautious awaiting key U.S. August jobs data due later for further clues on the direction of interest rates. The Hang Seng index ended down 14.92 points at 11,025.59 -- after falling to a low of 10,930.37 -- and was down 133.43 from last week.

SYDNEY - Australian shares ended mostly weaker, the market bruised by Thursday's nervous Dow ahead of the release of U.S. payroll data later today, although selective bargain hunting helped restrict the market's fall. The All Ordinaries index closed 20.4 points lower at 2,237.0, a fall of 31.7 since last Friday.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares ended a touch firmer after a patchy day due to a five hour stoppage of trade due to an electronic trading system malfuntion. Golds ended weak on a dull bullion price. Trade was extended for an hour after usual closing time. Dealers said the market anticipated a weaker Wall Street after the strong payroll figures in the U.S. but were surprised by a strong Wall Street at local close. The Overall index fell 3.5 points to 6,786.1, rising 97.2 from last week, the Industrial index rose 5.6 points to 7,975.9, up 140.7 from a week ago and the Gold index slipped 14.2 points to 1,782.6, falling five from last Friday.
